# ScreenR <a href="https://emanuelsoda.github.io/ScreenR/"><img src="man/figures/logo.png" align="right" height="139" alt="ScreenR logo" /></a>

<!-- badges: start -->
[![Bioconductor release](https://bioconductor.org/shields/years-in-bioc/ScreenR.svg)](https://bioconductor.org/packages/ScreenR)
[![Bioc release build](https://bioconductor.org/shields/build/release/bioc/ScreenR.svg)](https://bioconductor.org/checkResults/release/bioc-LATEST/ScreenR/)
[![Bioc devel build](https://bioconductor.org/shields/build/devel/bioc/ScreenR.svg)](https://bioconductor.org/checkResults/devel/bioc-LATEST/ScreenR/)
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/EmanuelSoda/ScreenR/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/EmanuelSoda/ScreenR/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/EmanuelSoda/ScreenR/branch/master/graph/badge.svg?token=NX5YVRP4L0)](https://codecov.io/gh/EmanuelSoda/ScreenR)
<!-- badges: end -->

**Find the genes that matter in pooled shRNA and CRISPR-Cas9 screens — with
p-values you can trust, quality control built in and publication-ready
plots.**

ScreenR takes the barcode counts (shRNAs or sgRNAs) of a pooled screen and
tells you which genes are depleted or enriched, by a treatment or over time,
how confident you can be in each of them, and whether the result holds up at
the level of the single barcodes. It is built on the statistics of
[edgeR](https://bioconductor.org/packages/edgeR) and
[limma](https://bioconductor.org/packages/limma), stores the data in a
Bioconductor `SummarizedExperiment`, and draws every plot with ggplot2.

<img src="man/figures/workflow.svg" alt="The ScreenR workflow" width="100%"/>

## Why ScreenR?

- **Every hit comes with a p-value and a false discovery rate.** The
  gene-level tests are calibrated: in screens without any real effect about
  5% of the genes have p < 0.05, as they should.
- **Benchmarked against the main tools.** On simulated screens and on
  published shRNA (K562) and CRISPR-Cas9 (HAP1) essentiality screens,
  ScreenR ranks the true hits as well as the best of MAGeCK, BAGEL2,
  gscreend and plain edgeR/limma workflows, keeps the FDR below the nominal
  level and runs in seconds
  ([benchmark](https://emanuelsoda.github.io/ScreenR/articles/Benchmark_MAGeCK.html)).
- **Several complementary methods, one table.** limma FRY, ROAST and CAMERA,
  a gene-level Z-score test with an empirical null (no reference genes
  needed), and tests across time points; `summarise_hits()` combines them and
  `plot_common_hit()` shows how they agree.
- **Uses your replicates.** Barcode statistics come from the edgeR
  quasi-likelihood model, so replicate variability is part of the test.
- **Quality control included.** Mapped reads, library evenness (Gini index),
  lost barcodes, replicate correlation and MDS plots, before you look at a
  single hit.
- **Works with your files as they are.** Any column names, sample
  descriptions from a table, helpful messages when something does not match.
- **shRNA and CRISPR.** Treated vs control screens and dropout screens with
  only time points; checks the screen with essential and non-essential
  reference genes (`compute_screen_quality()`), and corrects CRISPR
  copy-number bias through
  [CRISPRcleanR](https://github.com/francescojm/CRISPRcleanR)
  (`correct_crispr_bias()`).
- **Bioconductor native.** The ScreenR object is a `SummarizedExperiment`, so
  it works with the rest of the Bioconductor ecosystem.

## Installation

ScreenR requires R 4.3 or later. Install the release version from
[Bioconductor](https://bioconductor.org/packages/ScreenR):

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages("BiocManager")
}
BiocManager::install("ScreenR")
```

or the development version from GitHub:

```{r install-dev, eval = FALSE}
BiocManager::install("EmanuelSoda/ScreenR")
```

## Quick start

### A treated vs control shRNA screen

The package includes an example screen: shRNA counts of treated (`TRT`) and
control (`CTRL`) cells 7 and 14 days after the selection (`Time3` and
`Time4`), with three replicates, and two samples taken before the treatment.
ScreenR plots have no theme of their own: choose one once with `theme_set()`.

```{r packages, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
library(ScreenR)
library(ggplot2)
theme_set(theme_light())
```

Describe the samples with a `sample_table`, give the `groups` used by the
statistical models, and the colors of the conditions:

```{r quick-start, message = FALSE}
data(count_table)
data(annotation_table)
samples <- data.frame(
    Sample = c("Time1", "Time2", paste0(rep(c("Time3", "Time4"), each = 6),
        "_", rep(rep(c("TRT", "CTRL"), each = 3), 2), "_", c("A", "B", "C"))),
    Day = c("Time1", "Time2", rep(c("Time3", "Time4"), each = 6)),
    Treatment = c("Time1", "Time2", rep(rep(c("TRT", "CTRL"), each = 3), 2))
)
counts <- count_table[count_table$Barcode != "*", ]
colnames(counts) <- c("Barcode", samples$Sample)
groups <- factor(ifelse(samples$Day %in% c("Time1", "Time2"), "T1/T2",
    paste(samples$Day, samples$Treatment, sep = "_")))

object <- create_screenr_object(
    table = counts, annotation = annotation_table, groups = groups,
    sample_table = samples,
    palettes = list(
        Treatment = c(Time1 = "#CCCCCC", Time2 = "#999999",
            CTRL = "#1B9E77", TRT = "#D95F02"),
        Group = c(`T1/T2` = "#999999", Time3_CTRL = "#66C2A5",
            Time3_TRT = "#FC8D62", Time4_CTRL = "#1B9E77", Time4_TRT = "#D95F02")
    )
)
object <- normalize_data(remove_all_zero_row(object), method = "tmm")
object
```

Check the samples before looking for hits: replicates should cluster together.

```{r qc, fig.height = 3.5, fig.width = 7}
plot_mds(object)
```

Compare treated and control cells at the last time point with three
complementary tests, and combine them:

```{r hits}
design <- create_design_matrix(object)
contrast <- create_contrast(design, treatment = "Time4_TRT", control = "Time4_CTRL")

# Do the barcodes of each gene change? (limma FRY, recommended first test)
fry <- find_roast_hit(object, design, contrast, method = "fry", fdr = 1)
# Do they change more than the barcodes of the other genes? (limma CAMERA)
camera <- find_camera_hit(object, design, contrast, fdr = 1)
# Is the mean barcode score extreme? (Z-score test with an empirical null)
statistics <- compute_barcode_statistics(object, design, contrast)
zscore <- find_gene_zscore_hit(statistics, reference = "empirical", fdr = 1)

# One table with the FDR of every method, best supported genes first
# (the example screen has a weak effect, so a lenient FDR of 25% is used)
hits <- summarise_hits(list(fry = fry, camera = camera, zscore = zscore),
    fdr = 0.25)
head(hits)
```

Look at the top candidates in the data before trusting them: how far treated
and control cells separate at each time point after the treatment.

```{r top-gene, fig.height = 3.5, fig.width = 8}
treated_days <- samples$Sample[samples$Day %in% c("Time3", "Time4")]
plot_treatment_separation(object, genes = hits$Gene[1:3],
    treatment = "TRT", control = "CTRL", samples = treated_days, nrow = 1)
```

### A CRISPR-Cas9 dropout screen

A dropout screen has no treatment: the time points go in the `Day` column and
`compute_metrics(condition_column = "Day")` compares them. The core essential
genes of Hart et al. should be depleted, the non-essential genes not:

```{r crispr, message = FALSE}
data(hap1_count_table)
data(hap1_annotation_table)
data(hart_reference_genes)
days <- c("T0", "T3", "T3", "T3", "T18", "T18", "T18")
crispr <- create_screenr_object(
    table = hap1_count_table, annotation = hap1_annotation_table,
    groups = factor(days, levels = c("T0", "T3", "T18")),
    sample_table = data.frame(Sample = colnames(hap1_count_table)[-1],
        Day = days, Treatment = "Untreated"),
    palettes = list(Day = c(T0 = "#999999", T3 = "#7570B3", T18 = "#D95F02"))
)
crispr <- normalize_data(remove_all_zero_row(crispr))
day18 <- compute_metrics(crispr,
    control = "T0", treatment = "T18", condition_column = "Day")
essential <- hart_reference_genes$Gene[
    hart_reference_genes$Class == "core essential"]
nonessential <- hart_reference_genes$Gene[
    hart_reference_genes$Class == "non-essential"]
compute_screen_quality(day18, essential, nonessential)
```

```{r crispr-trend, fig.height = 3.5, fig.width = 8}
plot_treatment_separation(crispr, genes = c("POLR2L", "RPL14", "EGFP"),
    treatment = c("T3", "T18"), control = "T0", condition_column = "Day",
    time = c(T0 = 0, T3 = 3, T18 = 18), nrow = 1) +
    labs(x = "Days")
```

[Tutorial 4](https://emanuelsoda.github.io/ScreenR/articles/Tutorial_4_CRISPR_screens.html)
continues with the hits, the efficiency of the sgRNAs and the copy-number
correction.

## Which method should I use?

Every method looks for **depleted** genes by default; set
`direction = "Up"` to find **enriched** genes (for example in a resistance
screen).

| Question | Function | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Do the barcodes of a gene change? | `find_roast_hit(method = "fry")` | limma FRY, self-contained; the recommended first test. Needs replicates. |
| Do they change more than the barcodes of the other genes? | `find_camera_hit()` | limma CAMERA, competitive; works with a single control sample. |
| Is the mean barcode score of a gene extreme? | `compute_barcode_statistics()` + `find_gene_zscore_hit()` | Use `reference = "empirical"` when no reference genes are known, `control_genes =` with the non-essential genes of a CRISPR screen, and `statistic = "median"` against off-target effects. |
| Does the gene change at every time point? | `find_consistent_hit()` | Runs the same test for several contrasts. |
| Does the effect change over time? | `find_time_hit()` | Model of the whole time course, treated vs control. |
| Which genes are supported by several methods? | `summarise_hits()`, `find_common_hit()`, `plot_common_hit()` | One table with the FDR of every method. |

## How ScreenR compares

```{r benchmark, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, fig.height = 3.6, fig.width = 8}
library(ggplot2)
benchmark_dir <- system.file("extdata", "benchmark", package = "ScreenR")
bench <- rbind(
    read.csv(file.path(benchmark_dir, "simulation.csv")),
    read.csv(file.path(benchmark_dir, "simulation_competitors.csv"))
)
keep <- c(
    MAGeCK_RRA = "MAGeCK RRA", MAGeCK_MLE = "MAGeCK MLE",
    BAGEL2 = "BAGEL2", gscreend = "gscreend",
    limma_voom_camera = "limma-voom + camera",
    ScreenR_CAMERA = "ScreenR CAMERA",
    ScreenR_Zscore_mean = "ScreenR Z-score"
)
scenarios <- c(S1_baseline = "Baseline", S2_weak_effect = "Weak effect",
    S3_two_replicates = "2 replicates", S4_noisy = "Noisy",
    S5_off_target = "Off-target")
bench <- subset(bench, method %in% names(keep) & alpha == 0.05 &
    scenario %in% names(scenarios))
summary <- aggregate(cbind(AUPRC, FDP) ~ method + scenario, bench, mean)
summary$Method <- factor(keep[summary$method], levels = keep)
summary$Scenario <- factor(scenarios[summary$scenario], levels = scenarios)
ggplot(summary, aes(Scenario, AUPRC, fill = Method)) +
    geom_col(position = position_dodge(0.8), width = 0.75) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.5, 1)) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("#E3A894", "#B5523A", "#5B4E9E", "#D4A72C",
        "#9ECAE9", "#93B5A3", "#1F5F55")) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Precision-recall AUC", fill = NULL,
        title = "Ranking of the true hits in 25 simulated screens") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.major.x = element_blank())
```

In the simulations ScreenR ranks the true hits as well as the best tools and
keeps the false discovery rate below the nominal level; at a fixed FDR it is
more conservative than MAGeCK MLE and BAGEL2, which find more hits but exceed
the nominal FDR in some scenarios. On the published K562 shRNA screen
included in the package (`k562_count_table`) the ScreenR Z-score test is
comparable to MAGeCK RRA and BAGEL2. The
[benchmark article](https://emanuelsoda.github.io/ScreenR/articles/Benchmark_MAGeCK.html)
has all the details and reruns the ScreenR side of the comparison.

| | |
|---|---|
| [Tutorial 1: Getting your data into ScreenR](https://emanuelsoda.github.io/ScreenR/articles/Tutorial_1_Creating_the_object.html) | Count tables, annotations, sample descriptions and the ScreenR object |
| [Tutorial 2: Quality control](https://emanuelsoda.github.io/ScreenR/articles/Tutorial_2_Quality_control.html) | Sequencing depth, library evenness, replicates, normalization |
| [Tutorial 3: Finding and validating hits](https://emanuelsoda.github.io/ScreenR/articles/Tutorial_3_Finding_hits.html) | All the hit-finding methods, combining them and checking the hits |
| [Tutorial 4: CRISPR-Cas9 screens](https://emanuelsoda.github.io/ScreenR/articles/Tutorial_4_CRISPR_screens.html) | Dropout screens over time, sgRNA thresholds and efficiency, quality with reference genes, copy-number correction with CRISPRcleanR, hits |
| [Statistics in ScreenR](https://emanuelsoda.github.io/ScreenR/articles/Improved_Statistics.html) | How the tests work and why |
| [Choosing the reference of the gene-level test](https://emanuelsoda.github.io/ScreenR/articles/Empirical_null.html) | Why we suggest `find_gene_zscore_hit(reference = "empirical")` |
| [Benchmark against MAGeCK and other tools](https://emanuelsoda.github.io/ScreenR/articles/Benchmark_MAGeCK.html) | Simulations, an shRNA and a CRISPR screen with known hits, compared with MAGeCK, BAGEL2, gscreend and edgeR/limma |
